sentence_stem: Of all the cities we visited,
full_sentence: Of all the cities we visited, Rome was the most beautiful.
acceptable_variants: Rome was the most beautiful city of all.
Rome was the most beautiful of them all.

options.why_wrong: This is a true statement, but it does not compare the cities, so it does not complete the superlative comparison started by 'of all'.

options.text: Rome was more beautiful than Paris.
options.why_wrong: This uses the comparative form 'more beautiful', which compares two cities. The stem with 'of all' needs the superlative form to rank one city above the whole group.
This describes the trains, not the cities, so it does not complete the comparison the stem sets up.

explanation: The phrase 'of all' introduces a whole group, so the sentence needs a superlative adjective such as 'the most beautiful' to rank one item above the others. Portuguese speakers may be tempted to use a comparative form like 'more beautiful' here, but English requires 'the most' when one item is compared with a whole group.
translation: De todas as cidades que visitamos, Roma foi a mais bonita.
